name: Frigate
summary: Security cameras: records your IP cameras and spots people, cars and animals in them, all on the NAS

options.label: Recordings folder
options.help: Where Frigate keeps its recordings, clips and snapshots - on a share, so they can also be copied off over SMB. Frigate deletes old recordings itself (after 7 days by default, alerts and detections after 30). A new, empty folder.

options.label: Object detection
options.help: What spots people, cars and animals. The NAS's own processor manages one or two quiet cameras; a Coral USB accelerator (plugged into the NAS) or another machine on your network (e.g. a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8L, or a PC) handles 4-8. Manual: the detectors and model sections of Frigate's own settings are left as you've set them.

choices.label: Coral USB accelerator, plugged into the NAS
Another machine on the network (Frigate's remote detector)

options.label: Remote detector address
options.help: For "Another machine": its address and port, e.g. 192.168.1.50:5555 - where the recipe's detector server runs (see the recipe's README: remote-detector). It's asked which model it uses when the settings are saved, so it must be running then.

options.label: Admin password
options.help: For Frigate's admin user (admin). It can be changed later in Frigate (Settings -> Users).

options.label: Frigate version
options.help: The Frigate release to run. A remote detector should run the same version.
